goal.objective:
Finish `src/trie.js`, whose `Trie` class currently keeps words in a plain map. Build a real trie: one node per distinct prefix, walked by Unicode code point so a character outside the basic plane is a single step and never a pair of surrogate halves. Every listing is ordered by code point, so `'\uFF10'` comes before `'\uFFFD'` and both come before an emoji. You may add files under `src/`.

`insert(word, value)` stores a value and returns the value it replaced, or `undefined` when the word is new. `get(word)` and `has(word)` read it back. `delete(word)` removes a word, returns whether it removed one, and drops the nodes that word alone kept alive; deleting a string that is only a prefix of stored words removes nothing and returns `false`. `countPrefix(prefix)` returns how many stored words start with the prefix, and must cost the length of the prefix rather than a walk of the subtree, so keep a per-node count of the words below it. `search(prefix, limit)` lists the matching words in order, at most `limit` of them, defaulting to no limit; a prefix that is not in the index yields an empty list. `entries()` lists every `[word, value]` pair in order. `longestPrefixMatch(text)` returns `{ word, value }` for the longest stored word that is a prefix of `text`, or `null` when no stored word is.

The empty string is an ordinary word: it can be stored, it is a prefix of every string, and `countPrefix('')` is the number of stored words. `size` is the number of stored words. `nodeCount` counts nodes including the root, so an empty index has a node count of 1 and, after any sequence of inserts and deletes, the count equals the number of distinct prefixes of the stored words plus that root.

A word, prefix, or text argument that is not a string raises `TypeError` with message `word must be a string`, `prefix must be a string`, or `text must be a string` respectively. A limit that is neither `Infinity` nor a non-negative safe integer raises `TypeError` with message `limit must be a non-negative integer`. Do not add dependencies; `test/` and `package.json` are fixed and the suite must pass with `node --test test/*.test.js`. Change only files under src/. Do not modify anything under test/ or package.json, and add no dependencies: node_modules must not exist. The standard is `node --test test/*.test.js` passing in the workspace root.

You are an AI agent powered by DeepSeek Harness.

You implement one program task in the workspace you are given, against its own test suite, and you stop when the tests pass.

Use the read tool — not shell commands like cat — to inspect text files. Results include line numbers. Use offset and limit to continue reading large files.

Use the write tool to create files or completely replace file contents. Existing files are overwritten, so read an existing file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it) and prefer edit for targeted changes.

Use the edit tool for targeted changes to existing UTF-8 text files. It replaces literal old_string with new_string; by default old_string must appear exactly once. If old_string appears multiple times, provide a more specific old_string or set replace_all to true. Read the file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it), unless you just created or edited it in this session.

Check the [exit code: N] marker on every bash result; investigate failures before moving on.

Track every background job id you start. You are notified in-session when a job finishes — do not busy-poll or sleep on one; keep working on independent steps and do not duplicate a running job's work. Before giving a final answer, collect every still-relevant job with job_output (set wait: true only when you are genuinely blocked on it), and job_kill jobs that stopped mattering.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.description: Load the full instructions for an available skill. Call this with the exact skill name from the session skill catalog before acting on a task that names or clearly matches that skill.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

1: import { test } from 'node:test';
2: import assert from 'node:assert/strict';

4: import { Trie } from '../src/trie.js';
5: 
6: /**
7:  * Deterministic 32-bit PRNG.
8:  * @param {number} seed Initial state.
9:  * @returns {() => number} Generator returning floats in [0, 1).
10:  */
11: function mulberry32(seed) {
12:   let a = seed >>> 0;
13:   return () => {
14:     a = (a + 0x6d2b79f5) >>> 0;
15:     let t = Math.imul(a ^ (a >>> 15), 1 | a);
16:     t = (t + Math.imul(t ^ (t >>> 7), 61 | t)) ^ t;
17:     return ((t ^ (t >>> 14)) >>> 0) / 4294967296;
18:   };
19: }
20: 
21: /**
22:  * Compares two strings by Unicode code point.
23:  * @param {string} a First string.
24:  * @param {string} b Second string.
25:  * @returns {number} Negative, zero, or positive.
26:  */
27: function byCodePoint(a, b) {
28:   const left = [...a];
29:   const right = [...b];
30:   for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(left.length, right.length); i += 1) {
31:     const diff = left[i].codePointAt(0) - right[i].codePointAt(0);
32:     if (diff !== 0) return diff;
33:   }
34:   return left.length - right.length;
35: }
36: 
37: /**
38:  * Every distinct prefix of a set of words, the empty prefix included.
39:  * @param {Iterable<string>} words Stored words.
40:  * @returns {Set<string>} Distinct prefixes.
41:  */
42: function prefixesOf(words) {
43:   const out = new Set(['']);
44:   for (const word of words) {
45:     const chars = [...word];
46:     for (let i = 1; i <= chars.length; i += 1) out.add(chars.slice(0, i).join(''));
47:   }
48:   return out;
49: }

51: test('an empty trie holds nothing but its root', () => {
52:   const trie = new Trie();
53:   assert.deepEqual([trie.size, trie.nodeCount], [0, 1]);
54:   assert.deepEqual([trie.has('a'), trie.get('a'), trie.delete('a')], [false, undefined, false]);
55:   assert.deepEqual([trie.countPrefix(''), trie.search(''), trie.entries()], [0, [], []]);
56:   assert.equal(trie.longestPrefixMatch('anything'), null);
57: });

60:   const trie = new Trie();
61:   assert.equal(trie.insert('cat', 1), undefined);
62:   assert.equal(trie.insert('car', 2), undefined);
63:   assert.equal(trie.insert('cat', 3), 1);
64:   assert.deepEqual([trie.get('cat'), trie.get('car'), trie.get('ca')], [3, 2, undefined]);
65:   assert.deepEqual([trie.size, trie.nodeCount], [2, 5]);
66:   assert.deepEqual([trie.has('cat'), trie.has('ca'), trie.has('cats')], [true, false, false]);
67:   assert.equal(trie.insert('', 'root'), undefined);
68:   assert.deepEqual([trie.size, trie.nodeCount, trie.has(''), trie.get('')], [3, 5, true, 'root']);
69: });

72:   const trie = new Trie();
73:   for (const word of ['cat', 'car', 'cart', 'dog']) trie.insert(word, word.length);
74:   assert.deepEqual([trie.size, trie.nodeCount], [4, 9]);

76:   assert.equal(trie.delete('cat'), true);
77:   assert.deepEqual([trie.size, trie.nodeCount, trie.has('cat')], [3, 8, false]);
78:   assert.equal(trie.delete('cat'), false);
79:   assert.equal(trie.delete('cart'), true);
80:   assert.deepEqual([trie.size, trie.nodeCount], [2, 7]);

All 9 tests pass. The implementation is complete:

- **`src/trie.js`** now implements a real trie with one `Node` per distinct prefix, keyed by Map entries of single Unicode code points (via `Array.from(string)`, which correctly splits by code point rather than UTF-16 code unit — so astral characters like `\u{1F600}` are single steps, not surrogate pairs).
- Each node tracks a `count` of words in its subtree, updated incrementally on insert/delete, giving `countPrefix` O(prefix length) cost instead of a subtree walk.
- `nodeCount`/`size` are maintained as counters rather than recomputed.
- `delete` walks the path, clears the end marker, decrements counts along the path, and prunes any trailing nodes whose count drops to 0 (but stops at the first node still needed).
- Listings (`search`, `entries`) walk children sorted by `codePointAt(0)` to guarantee code-point ordering (so `\uFF10 < \uFFFD < \u{1F600}`).
- `longestPrefixMatch` walks the text by code point, tracking the last node seen where `isEnd` was true.
- All type/limit validation matches the required `TypeError` messages exactly.

The test suite (`node --test test/*.test.js`) reports 9/9 passing, including the long randomized cross-check against a plain `Map` model over 3000 operations. Only `src/trie.js` was modified; `test/` and `package.json` were left untouched, and no dependencies/`node_modules` were introduced.

goal.objective:
Finish `src/trie.js`, whose `Trie` class currently keeps words in a plain map. Build a real trie: one node per distinct prefix, walked by Unicode code point so a character outside the basic plane is a single step and never a pair of surrogate halves. Every listing is ordered by code point, so `'\uFF10'` comes before `'\uFFFD'` and both come before an emoji. You may add files under `src/`.

`insert(word, value)` stores a value and returns the value it replaced, or `undefined` when the word is new. `get(word)` and `has(word)` read it back. `delete(word)` removes a word, returns whether it removed one, and drops the nodes that word alone kept alive; deleting a string that is only a prefix of stored words removes nothing and returns `false`. `countPrefix(prefix)` returns how many stored words start with the prefix, and must cost the length of the prefix rather than a walk of the subtree, so keep a per-node count of the words below it. `search(prefix, limit)` lists the matching words in order, at most `limit` of them, defaulting to no limit; a prefix that is not in the index yields an empty list. `entries()` lists every `[word, value]` pair in order. `longestPrefixMatch(text)` returns `{ word, value }` for the longest stored word that is a prefix of `text`, or `null` when no stored word is.

The empty string is an ordinary word: it can be stored, it is a prefix of every string, and `countPrefix('')` is the number of stored words. `size` is the number of stored words. `nodeCount` counts nodes including the root, so an empty index has a node count of 1 and, after any sequence of inserts and deletes, the count equals the number of distinct prefixes of the stored words plus that root.

A word, prefix, or text argument that is not a string raises `TypeError` with message `word must be a string`, `prefix must be a string`, or `text must be a string` respectively. A limit that is neither `Infinity` nor a non-negative safe integer raises `TypeError` with message `limit must be a non-negative integer`. Do not add dependencies; `test/` and `package.json` are fixed and the suite must pass with `node --test test/*.test.js`. Change only files under src/.
